NMDA receptor gating – uncovered. Banke and Tray
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the NR1 and NR-2 subunits of NMDA receptors have different gating mechanisms.
the NMDA receptor channel pore is a composite of the NR1 and NR subunits, and the NR2 subunit is the dominant determinant of receptor kinetics.
the NR1 and NR1/NR2 subunits are the major contributors to NMDAR gating, whereas the NR2 subunits play only a minor role in channel opening.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the gating of NMDA receptors can be described in terms of two kinetically distinct processes.
the NMDA receptor channel is a composite of two kinetically distinct gates, one that is controlled by the NR1 subunit and another that is controlled by NR2 subunits.
the NMDA receptor is a highly cooperative receptor.
